"Stitched up" by Herne Hill's Taylor Fine weather, a good course and strong rivalry between local clubs led to an exciting race.

Hounslow's Farah made a bold bid to escape at the front but there was no denying Taylor's gut-wrenching burst up the finishing hill. Sadly Farah's name was later to be removed from the official result because at 16 years of age he should not have been running in the senior event.

It did seem that way, for the flag was surrounded by "class" athletes pulling on Belgrave racing strip, and when the runners charged up the playing fields and off into the woods, a blur of claret and gold vests was prominent around the red and black of Dave Taylor's Herne Hill kit.

Mark Miles looked in fine fettle and sure enough, as the leaders broke away from the field, he was tucked in nicely behind Herne Hill's Dave Taylor with our own Geremew Wolde, Yitbarak Dinku and Paul Freary in close attendance.

But two miles into the race it was Boxhill's Paul Haywood who had taken the initiative, 30 metres up on Blackheath's Taylor who was in turn heading a bunch of seven runners that was being chased by Paul, 9th, and Lee 15th.

As the senior men's field assembled it was noted that Dave Taylor of Herne Hill was indeed taking part to give him a 100% turn-out record in the League, and Hounslow's Mike Simpson, fourth-placer from the previous week's "Southern", was also in the line-up.
Herne Hill's Dave Taylor continues to dominate cross country events in Surrey but in this Championship he did not have it completely his own way.
Herne Hill's ever-present Dave Taylor, the league's individual winner last winter, soon showed his intentions by opening up a lead which stretched to nearly a minute by the finish.
